questions.question: How big is the loan book and how did it move?
questions.answer: Total outstanding was ₹1,920.51 Cr at Dec 2025 (+₹25.86 Cr vs last month). +₹2.00 Cr vs previous quarter. +₹115.80 Cr vs last year. Main driver: 1.5 - 2.5 Cr (ticket size) accounted for 55% of the change in Total outstanding vs last month.

findings.text: Total outstanding rose ₹25.86 Cr vs last month to ₹1,920.51 Cr.
1.5 - 2.5 Cr (ticket size) accounted for 55% of the change in Total outstanding vs last month.

caveats: Outstanding is a month-end balance; months are compared, never added.

questions.question: What is the disbursement run-rate this fiscal year?
questions.answer: Disbursement amount was ₹518.63 Cr at FY26 YTD (−₹138.53 Cr vs last year to date). +₹6.79 Cr vs last month. −₹43.22 Cr vs last year. Main driver: DF-GF (product) accounted for 76% of the change in Disbursement amount vs last year to date.

findings.text: Disbursement amount fell ₹138.53 Cr vs last year to date to ₹518.63 Cr.
DF-GF (product) accounted for 76% of the change in Disbursement amount vs last year to date.

caveats: No disbursement plan or budget is available, so this is compared with last year, not with plan.

questions.question: What is the gross NPA ratio and what drove it?
questions.answer: Gross NPA ratio was 5.13% at Dec 2025 (-0.33 pp vs last month). -0.11 pp vs previous quarter. -0.90 pp vs last year. Main driver: DEMO-WEST (branch) moved Gross NPA ratio vs last month by more than the whole net change (114%); other segments partly offset it.

findings.text: Gross NPA ratio fell 0.33 pp vs last month to 5.13%.
DEMO-WEST (branch) moved Gross NPA ratio vs last month by more than the whole net change (114%); other segments partly offset it.
Closed / exited: −₹11.79 Cr (4 accounts), more than the whole net NPA outstanding movement (238%); other flows partly offset it.
By branch, the change is driven by rate (segments got worse or better): rate -0.31 pp, mix -0.02 pp.

caveats: NPA status is the lender's flag; reasons for slippage (borrower, economic) are not in the data.
Write-offs and closures reduce NPA mechanically.

questions.question: Are accounts slipping into later buckets faster?
questions.answer: No forward roll rate is materially above its 12-month average in Dec 2025. Key rates: Current → 1-30 DPD 1% (avg 1%); 61-90 DPD → 90+ DPD 50% (avg 77%).
caveats: Roll rates are month-on-month account transitions; small buckets make rates volatile.

questions.question: Which branches and states are deteriorating fastest?
questions.answer: Fastest deterioration vs last month: Tamil Nadu (state, 10% of the book): PAR 30+ ratio 11.32% → 12.16% (+0.85 pp).; DEMO-SOUTH (branch, 26% of the book): PAR 30+ ratio 3.26% → 3.44% (+0.18 pp).; Tamil Nadu (state, 10% of the book): Gross NPA ratio 10.56% → 12.16% (+1.61 pp).; DEMO-EAST (branch, 26% of the book): Gross NPA ratio 1.40% → 1.54% (+0.14 pp).

questions.question: How concentrated is our risk?
questions.answer: Top 3 states hold 58% of NPA outstanding; large tickets (above ₹2.5 Cr) are 43% of NPA; 3 accounts explain half of this month's NPA movement.
